subject: Performance validation kickoff — HavenAI post-demo: load test next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@haven.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Performance validation kickoff — HavenAI post-demo: load test next steps

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Recap of agreed scope:
- Target workload: streaming chat endpoint used by HavenAI’s in-product assistant (short session profile, median prompt ~60 tokens, median completion ~120 tokens).
- Primary SLOs you requested us to validate: p95 end-to-end latency <= 300ms for non-batched streaming completions; sustained throughput target 120 RPS; support for 40 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation beyond that.
- Duration: you suggested a 2-hour sustained window with a 30-minute ramp-up / ramp-down.

What we need from HavenAI to proceed:
1) Finalize test window (UTC preferred). Rishi proposed: 2027-07-23T02:00:00Z — 2027-07-23T04:00:00Z.
2) IP allowlist for test runners — please confirm CIDR blocks we should add (we will respond with Redwood ingress IPs once we receive yours).
3) Confirm whether you want exact p95 latency on per-request basis or per-token streaming latency (we can measure both).
4) Provide contact for on-call SRE during the window (name + mobile).

Attachments I’ve included: k6 script bundle (havenai-k6-scripts-v2.tar.gz) and a short runbook (redwood-runbook-k6.md). Ben has created a test API key and a sandbox account; see his note below for credentials and allowlist entries.

Next steps (quick):
- Samira: confirm test window + allowlist blocks by EOD tomorrow.
- Ben: share test account + monitoring links (copied).
- Lauren: standby for procurement checkpoint (MSA/PO) if we need to sign anything before the run.

If you prefer a different window or want a shorter dry-run first, let us know — we can do a 30–45 minute smoke run earlier this week.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

-----

From: Samira Khan <samira@haven.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@haven.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T17:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance validation kickoff — HavenAI post-demo: load test next steps

Thanks, Rishi — appreciate the clear summary.

Quick answers:
- 02:00–04:00 UTC on 2027-07-23 works for us (that aligns with an overnight window for our EU customers).
- Ramp plan: we want a 30-minute linear ramp to target, hold for 90 minutes, 30-minute ramp down (so total 2.5 hours). Is that doable?
- We’ll run the k6 scripts from our CI runners (AWS eu-west-1). Our SREs will provide the CIDR blocks — expecting to send them by EOD tomorrow.
- On-call: Tom Lee (tom.lee@haven.ai), mobile +44 7700 900123.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood provide a sandbox API key scoped to the test account (no billing triggers) and an expiry?
2) Want to confirm observability: will you expose structured traces and token-level timing to our Grafana link, or do we need to forward logs to our account?

We’d like to run a 15-minute smoke run 24 hours before the main window to validate allowlists and credentials.

—Samira
Head of Platform — HavenAI

-----

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@haven.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance validation kickoff — HavenAI post-demo: load test next steps

Hi Samira — I created the sandbox artifacts and added notes here. Short version below; full runbook is attached (redwood-runbook-k6.md) and the k6 bundle contains a README with knobs for streaming vs non-streaming modes.

Sandbox credentials (ephemeral):
- Account: havenai-sandbox-2027
- Test API key (read+infer scope, expires 2027-07-26): rk_test_havenai_9f3b**** (please treat as credential stub; we will rotate after the run)
- Endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streaming

IP allowlist (Redwood ingress expects these from runners):
- Added: 52.17.0.0/20 (example AWS eu-west-1 runners) — we will add more once you confirm additional ranges.
- Your allowlist (please confirm exact CIDRs) should include our runtime egress so your monitoring callbacks can reach your endpoints: 34.200.32.0/19

k6 bundle notes:
- Scripts provided: havenai_streaming_profile.js (streaming socket emulation), havenai_short_session.js (batch request emulation), harness/monitoring_integration.js (pushes metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana).
- Recommended test parameters for your target SLOs:
  * Ramp: 30 minutes linear to 120 RPS
  * Steady: 90 minutes at 120 RPS (approx. 40 concurrent streaming sessions depending on per-session token rate)
  * Ramp down: 30 minutes
  * Arrival rate mode (k6) preferred — avoids artificial synchronization of requests.

Observability / dashboards:
- Grafana (read-only dashboard for HavenAI): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/havenai/perf-ops
- We will stream traces to the dashboard and provide a trace link per anomalous request. Token-level timing is available as a secondary metric (sideloaded into the dashboard); if you need full raw traces we can provide a temporary S3 export.

Runbook highlights:
- Smoke run (15m) 2027-07-22T02:00:00Z — validate allowlist, key, basic latency.
- Main run 2027-07-23T02:00:00Z — 2027-07-23T04:00:00Z.
- On-call escalation: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.ai) +1 (415) 555-0147, backup: Lauren Bishop.

I’ve attached the k6 bundle and the runbook; the ip-allowlist-havenai.txt contains the runner CIDRs we expect you to provide. Let me know if you want the API key to be rate-limited further for safety.

—Ben
SRE, Redwood Inference

-----

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@haven.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance validation kickoff — HavenAI post-demo: load test next steps

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround, team. Confirming the plan and AOs (actions):

Confirmations:
- Smoke run: 2027-07-22T02:00:00Z (15 minutes) — HavenAI to provide CIDRs by 2027-07-21T23:59:00Z; Redwood will enable keys and add allowlist entries within 2 hours of receipt.
- Main run: 2027-07-23T02:00:00Z — 2027-07-23T04:00:00Z (30m ramp / 90m steady / 30m ramp-down).

Action owners and next steps:
- Samira: send final CIDR list and confirm if you want token-level timing as a primary metric or just p95 request latency. Deadline: 2027-07-21T23:59:00Z.
- Ben: finalize key rotation window and confirm whether the test API key will be automatically revoked at expiry (yes by default). Deadline: 2027-07-21T18:00:00Z.
- Lauren: confirm procurement/contract checklist (we may need a quick PO for the sandbox run if you want dedicated capacity). Deadline: 2027-07-21T17:00:00Z.

Pre-run checklist (short):
- Allowlist verified + smoke run successful.
- Grafana dashboard showing traces + metrics.
- Test artifacts uploaded to the HubSpot deal and shared with platform team: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/489

If all goes well, we’ll capture a post-run summary with p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput graphs, error breakdown by type, and recommended configuration (batching / quantization / routing tweaks) for HavenAI’s target workload. I’ll block time to review results with you the morning after the run — propose 2027-07-24T16:00:00Z for a 45-minute debrief.

Thanks — looking forward to the smoke run.

Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
